acceptance: morize-core exports exactly the planned durable identifier classes as distinct Rust types; no implicit cross-type conversion is implemented.
Every identifier has a canonical text length of 32 ASCII characters and Display emits lowercase hexadecimal only.
FromStr accepts exactly canonical lowercase 32-character hexadecimal input and rejects wrong length, uppercase input, and non-hexadecimal characters deterministically.
Fixed known byte values round-trip through every identifier type without changing bytes or canonical text.
cargo fmt --all -- --check passes on the exact implementation head.
cargo check --workspace --all-targets --offline passes on the exact implementation head.
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --offline -- -D warnings passes on the exact implementation head.
cargo test --workspace --all-targets --offline passes and includes focused identity tests for all planned identifier classes and rejection cases.
Cargo manifests and Cargo.lock are unchanged; the Grain admits no runtime, build, or test dependency.
GitHub Actions passes Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows on the exact implementation head before acceptance.
An independent semantic reviewer reviews the exact implementation head for identity-type separation, canonical-form strictness, scope containment, and required evidence.
ADR-0004 proof prerequisite for SG-000011 revalidates against the exact WorkPacket baseline before execution.
The implementation changes no path outside crates/morize-core/src/identity.rs and crates/morize-core/src/lib.rs.

method.control: Implementation is limited to typed identifier definitions, strict canonical text parsing/formatting, focused tests, and morize-core re-exports. No ID generation, persistence, serde, randomness, time semantics, or third-party dependency is authorized.
method.review_separation: An independent semantic reviewer must review the exact implementation head, identity semantics, and required evidence separately from the implementing agent before acceptance.
method.rollback: Revert the bounded typed-identifier implementation commits; no persisted Morize data or public stable release format exists yet.

minimality.rationale: A small standard-library-only typed-ID module inside the existing morize-core crate is the narrowest implementation. No crate split, donor code, serialization framework, random generator, or external dependency is required.

outcome: morize-core exposes non-interchangeable typed durable identifiers with one strict canonical textual representation and deterministic validation, without adding identifier generation, persistence, serde, or third-party dependencies.
rationale: MZ-DATA-001 and DATA_MODEL identity rules require stable typed identity before higher-level domain contracts. This Grain fixes only the in-memory typed identifier/value boundary and canonical text form so later serialization, storage, policy, and mutation Grains can build on one deterministic identity contract.

risk.recovery: Revert the bounded typed-identifier implementation commits; no persistent format or user data has been written by this Grain.

scope_in: Define distinct public newtypes for VaultId, PrincipalId, ScopeId, SourceId, ObservationId, EvidenceId, PropositionId, MemoryId, MemoryVersionId, RelationId, DecisionId, MutationId, PolicyRevisionId, BranchId, SnapshotId, ProjectionGenerationId, ContextBundleId, and ConnectorBindingId.
Represent each identifier as an opaque fixed 16-byte value while exposing only type-safe construction/access and strict canonical text parsing/formatting.
Define one canonical textual representation: exactly 32 lowercase hexadecimal ASCII characters with deterministic equality, ordering, hashing, Display, Debug, and FromStr behavior.
Add a bounded public parse-error type for invalid length and non-canonical/invalid hexadecimal input.
Add focused standard-library-only tests covering all identifier classes, canonical round trips, invalid length, uppercase rejection, invalid characters, and stable formatting.
scope_out: Identifier generation, randomness, UUID/ULID version semantics, clocks, monotonicity, database allocation, or collision-management services.
Serde or other serialization-framework integration, persisted field schemas, vault formats, migrations, configuration formats, or public API wire schemas.
Content digests, idempotency keys, timestamps, domain memory records, policy, authorization, retrieval, MCP, storage, or model behavior.
title: Define typed durable identifier values
